newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares tumble at close, programme sales.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares tumble at close, programme sales.

text.p: Singapore shares tumbled at the close on Thursday, pressured by programme selling of index-linked stocks, dealers said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index slumped 34.06 points to end at 1,989.80 after it broke its psychological support of 2,000.
Soft drink company Yeo Hiap Seng led the fall, ending 55 cents (US$0.38) down to S$5.05 on 37,000 shares.
"Yeo Hiap Seng, which normally trades around S$5.00, was ramped up to S$5.70 the last couple of days for no reason. I think someone just took profit," an analyst said.
Dealers said the more vibrant Hong Kong market continued to outshine Singapore, luring funds away.

Index-linked shipyards Sembawang and Keppel fell S$0.30 and S$0.10 respectively to end at S$6.55 and S$6.45. A dealer said lack of news on Keppel's plans to redevelop a site into a residential project was dampening its earnings outlook.
Infrastructure-based Van der Horst, which ended 22 cents up at S$2.70, was the most active with over 17.4 million shares traded.

Continued interest was seen for small-capitalised stocks like Excel Machine, which hit another new year high for the fourth consecutive day. It traded to S$0.825 before ending at S$0.805, up three cents.
